iterations.theme: Sveci su pobjednici – razmatranje čitanja iz 7. poglavlja knjige Otkrivenja na svetkovinu Svih svetih i povezanost s Dušnim danom

sections.subtitle: Svetkovina Svih svetih na dan Gospodnji
sections.screenshot_description: Fra Domagoj Runje pozdravlja gledatelje i najavljuje da svetkovina Svih svetih pada na nedjelju
sections.content:
Nakon kratkog uvodnog isječka u kojem se čuje nepoznati govornik s talijanskim pozdravom „Buonasera“, nova epizoda emisije *Škola Riječi* počinje tradicionalnim pozdravom „Hvaljen Isus i Marija“. Voditelj **fra Domagoj Runje** odmah ističe okolnost koja ovogodišnjem slavlju daje posebnu težinu: svetkovina Svih svetih pada u nedjelju, na **dan Gospodnji**.

Fra Domagoj najavljuje da će se u razmišljanju osvrnuti na prvo čitanje koje Crkva naviješta na tu svetkovinu. Riječ je o odlomku iz **7. poglavlja knjige Otkrivenja**, u kojem vidjelac Ivan opisuje viđenje na nebu. Upravo taj tekst, slikovit i bogat simbolima, okosnica je cijele epizode.
sections.subtitle_en: The Solemnity of All Saints on the Lord's Day
sections.screenshot_description_en: Fra Domagoj Runje greets the viewers and announces that the Solemnity of All Saints falls on a Sunday
sections.content_en:
After a short introductory clip in which an unknown speaker is heard with the Italian greeting “Buonasera”, the new episode of the show *Škola Riječi* begins with the traditional greeting “Praised be Jesus and Mary”. The host **fra Domagoj Runje** immediately highlights a circumstance that gives special weight to this year's celebration: the Solemnity of All Saints falls on Sunday, on the **Lord's day**.

Fra Domagoj announces that in the reflection he will look back at the first reading that the Church proclaims on that solemnity. It is a passage from **Chapter 7 of the Book of Revelation**, in which the visionary John describes a vision in heaven. That very text, vivid and rich in symbols, is the backbone of the entire episode.

sections.subtitle: Dva dijela knjige: viđenja na zemlji i viđenja na nebu
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj objašnjava podjelu knjige Otkrivenja na viđenja na zemlji i viđenja na nebu
sections.content:
Kako bi slušatelje uveo u tekst, fra Domagoj Runje najprije opisuje strukturu knjige Otkrivenja, koja se dijeli na dva glavna dijela:

- **Prva tri poglavlja**: vidjelac Ivan ima viđenja na zemlji.
- **Od 4. poglavlja do kraja knjige**: otvara se nebo i Ivan ima viđenja na nebu. Vidi što se ondje događa, ali s neba promatra i ono što se zbiva na zemlji.

Voditelj priznaje da se ti tekstovi čitatelju na prvi pogled mogu činiti kompliciranima. Ipak, smatra da se, kada se knjiga Otkrivenja čita **polako, dio po dio**, može ući u razumijevanje slika i simbola kojima je prožeta. Takvim strpljivim čitanjem vodi i slušatelje kroz odlomak.
sections.subtitle_en: Two Parts of the Book: Visions on Earth and Visions in Heaven
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host explains the division of the Book of Revelation into visions on earth and visions in heaven
sections.content_en:
In order to introduce the listeners to the text, fra Domagoj Runje first describes the structure of the Book of Revelation, which is divided into two main parts:

- **The first three chapters**: the visionary John has visions on earth.
- **From Chapter 4 to the end of the book**: heaven opens and John has visions in heaven. He sees what is happening there, but from heaven he also observes what is happening on earth.

The host admits that these texts may seem complicated to the reader at first glance. Nevertheless, he considers that, when the Book of Revelation is read **slowly, part by part**, one can enter into the understanding of the images and symbols with which it is permeated. Through such patient reading, he also guides the listeners through the passage.
keywords_en: structure of the Book of Revelation

sections.subtitle: Knjiga koja se „događa u nedjelju“
sections.screenshot_description: Fra Domagoj Runje govori o izrazu „dan Gospodnji“ i progonstvu vidioca Ivana na Patmosu
sections.content:
Zašto se ove godine razmišljanje o Svim svetima veže upravo uz knjigu Otkrivenja? Fra Domagoj Runje objašnjava da je razlog upravo u tome što svetkovina pada u nedjelju, a knjiga Otkrivenja, kako se slikovito izražava, „događa se u nedjelju“.

Knjiga Otkrivenja, naime, prema njegovim riječima, **najstariji je kršćanski spis u kojem se nalazi izraz „dan Gospodnji“**. Viđenja koja vidjelac Ivan prima događaju se upravo na dan Gospodnji, kada je pao u zanos na **otoku Patmosu**, gdje je bio u progonstvu.

Nakon tog uvoda voditelj čita cijeli odlomak: anđeo koji uzlazi od istoka sunčeva s pečatom Boga živoga zabranjuje četvorici anđela da naude zemlji i moru dok sluge Božje ne budu opečaćene na čelima. Slijedi broj od sto četrdeset i četiri tisuće opečaćenih iz svih plemena Izraelovih, a potom prizor **velikog mnoštva koje nitko ne može izbrojiti**, iz svakoga naroda, plemena, puka i jezika. Mnoštvo stoji pred prijestoljem i pred Jaganjcem u bijelim haljinama, s palmama u rukama, i kliče: „Spasenje Bogu našemu koji sjedi na prijestolju i Jaganjcu!“ Odlomak završava pitanjem jednog od starješina tko su ti u bijelim haljinama i odgovorom da su došli iz nevolje velike te su oprali i ubijelili svoje haljine u krvi Jaganjčevoj.
sections.screenshot_description_en: Fra Domagoj Runje speaks about the expression “Lord's day” and the exile of the visionary John on Patmos
sections.content_en:
Why is this year's reflection on All Saints tied specifically to the Book of Revelation? Fra Domagoj Runje explains that the reason is precisely that the solemnity falls on Sunday, and the Book of Revelation, as he vividly puts it, “happens on Sunday”.

The Book of Revelation, namely, according to his words, **is the oldest Christian writing in which the expression “Lord's day” is found**. The visions that the visionary John receives happen precisely on the Lord's day, when he fell into ecstasy on the **island of Patmos**, where he was in exile.

After that introduction, the host reads the entire passage: the angel who ascends from the rising of the sun with the seal of the living God forbids the four angels to harm the earth and the sea until the servants of God are sealed on their foreheads. There follows the number of one hundred and forty-four thousand sealed from all the tribes of Israel, and then the scene of a **great multitude that no one could count**, from every nation, tribe, people, and tongue. The multitude stands before the throne and before the Lamb in white robes, with palm branches in their hands, and cries out: “Salvation belongs to our God who sits on the throne and to the Lamb!” The passage ends with the question of one of the elders as to who these are in white robes and the answer that they came out of the great tribulation and washed and whitened their robes in the blood of the Lamb.

sections.subtitle: Anđeo s pečatom i prizor prije konačnog suda
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj tumači prizor anđela koji zaustavlja ostale anđele prije konačnog suda
sections.content:
Fra Domagoj Runje poziva slušatelje da obrate pozornost na likove koji se pojavljuju u odlomku. Prvi je anđeo koji se obraća ostalim anđelima i zaustavlja ih: neka ne naude ni moru ni zemlji dok ne budu opečaćene sluge Boga.

Prema njegovu tumačenju, riječ je o prizoru koji se odvija **prije konačnog suda svijeta**. Opečaćeni će biti oni koji se nazivaju slugama Božjim, odnosno oni koji su na ovom svijetu **vršili volju Božju**. Upravo će oni, ističe voditelj, imati udio u **Kristovoj konačnoj pobjedi dobra nad zlom**.
sections.subtitle_en: The Angel with the Seal and the Scene Before the Final Judgment
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host interprets the scene of the angel stopping the other angels before the final judgment
sections.content_en:
Fra Domagoj Runje invites listeners to pay attention to the figures appearing in the passage. The first is an angel who addresses the other angels and stops them: let them harm neither the sea nor the earth until the servants of God are sealed.

According to his interpretation, it is a scene taking place **before the final judgment of the world**. Those sealed will be those who are called servants of God, that is, those who on this world **did the will of God**. It is precisely they, the host points out, who will have a share in **Christ's final victory of good over evil**.

sections.subtitle: Tajna broja 144.000 i nebeska liturgija
sections.screenshot_description: Fra Domagoj Runje objašnjava simboliku broja 12 i 24 starješine
sections.content:
Posebnu pozornost voditelj posvećuje broju od **sto četrdeset i četiri tisuće opečaćenih** iz svih plemena sinova Izraelovih. Naglašava da je to **simboličan broj**, izveden iz broja 12.

Broj 12 u Bibliji općenito, a u ovom kontekstu knjige Otkrivenja na poseban način, označava **spoj staroga i novoga Božjega naroda**:

- 12 simbolizira **12 plemena Izraelovih**,
- ali i **12 Jaganjčevih apostola**.

Zbroj 12 i 12 daje 24, a i taj se broj pojavljuje u knjizi Otkrivenja. Odnosi se na **24 starješine** oko prijestolja Božjega i Jaganjčeva, koji predstavljaju 24 svećenička razreda iz starozavjetnog hramskog bogoslužja. Razlog je, objašnjava fra Domagoj, to što se na nebu neprestano odvija **nebeska liturgija** u kojoj cijelo stvorenje slavi Boga. Pred čitateljem je tako liturgijski prizor u kojem sudjeluje veliko mnoštvo opečaćenih.
sections.subtitle_en: The Mystery of the Number 144,000 and the Heavenly Liturgy
sections.screenshot_description_en: Fra Domagoj Runje explains the symbolism of the number 12 and the 24 elders
sections.content_en:
The host devotes special attention to the number of **one hundred and forty-four thousand sealed** from all the tribes of the sons of Israel. He emphasizes that this is a **symbolic number**, derived from the number 12.

The number 12 in the Bible in general, and in this context of the Book of Revelation in a special way, signifies the **union of the old and the new people of God**:

- 12 symbolizes the **12 tribes of Israel**,
- but also the **12 apostles of the Lamb**.

The sum of 12 and 12 gives 24, and that number also appears in the Book of Revelation. It refers to the **24 elders** around the throne of God and of the Lamb, who represent the 24 priestly classes from the Old Testament temple worship. The reason, fra Domagoj explains, is that in heaven a **heavenly liturgy** takes place unceasingly in which all creation praises God. Before the reader is thus a liturgical scene in which the great multitude of the sealed participates.

sections.subtitle: Optimizam Apokalipse: većina ljudi je dobra
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj ističe optimizam knjige Otkrivenja i dobrotu većine ljudi
sections.content:
Broj 144.000, prema tumačenju fra Domagoja Runjea, označava veliko mnoštvo onih iz Božjega izabranoga naroda, što znači da će se **mnogi spasiti**. No spašeni neće biti samo oni iz 12 plemena Izraelovih. Uz njih je i **neizbrojivo mnoštvo iz svakoga naroda i plemena i puka i jezika**.

Zato voditelj zaključuje da je pisac knjige Otkrivenja **izrazito optimističan**. Iako knjiga na pojedinim mjestima zvuči zastrašujuće, toliko da su riječ *apokalipsa* i pridjev *apokaliptički* postali sinonimi za katastrofe, ona zapravo s velikim optimizmom govori o neizbrojivom mnoštvu spašenih, onih koji su se u ovom svijetu pokazali kao sluge Božje.

U tome fra Domagoj vidi istinu koja, kako kaže, možda nije toliko očita ni popularna i o kojoj se rijetko govori: **na ovom svijetu većina ljudi ipak je dobra**, većina želi dobro i želi živjeti u miru, ljubavi i slozi. Knjiga Otkrivenja time donosi pravu evanđeosku, radosnu poruku.
sections.subtitle_en: The Optimism of the Apocalypse: Most People Are Good
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host highlights the optimism of the Book of Revelation and the goodness of the majority of people
sections.content_en:
The number 144,000, according to the interpretation of fra Domagoj Runje, signifies a great multitude of those from God's chosen people, which means that **many will be saved**. But the saved will not be only those from the 12 tribes of Israel. Alongside them is also an **innumerable multitude from every nation and tribe and people and tongue**.

Therefore, the host concludes that the author of the Book of Revelation is **extremely optimistic**. Although the book sounds terrifying in certain places, so much so that the word *apocalypse* and the adjective *apocalyptic* have become synonyms for catastrophes, it actually speaks with great optimism about the innumerable multitude of the saved, those who in this world showed themselves to be servants of God.

In this, fra Domagoj sees a truth that, as he says, is perhaps not so obvious or popular and about which one rarely speaks: **in this world most people are nevertheless good**, the majority wants good and wants to live in peace, love, and harmony. The Book of Revelation thereby brings a true evangelical, joyful message.

sections.subtitle: Prijestolje i Jaganjac: slika istobitnosti Oca i Sina
sections.screenshot_description: Fra Domagoj Runje tumači odnos Onoga koji sjedi na prijestolju i Jaganjca
sections.content:
Mnoštvo stoji pred prijestoljem i pred Jaganjcem. Fra Domagoj Runje upozorava na motiv koji se provlači kroz cijelu knjigu Otkrivenja: kada se govori o nebeskom, Božjem prijestolju, spominju se **Onaj koji sjedi na prijestolju** i **Jaganjac**, koji mu je jednak. Obojici se, naime, uvijek iskazuje **ista čast**.

Svi koji se klanjaju Onome koji sjedi na prijestolju klanjaju se i Jaganjcu. Voditelj ističe da ne postoji tekst u kojem bi se Jaganjac klanjao Onome na prijestolju. Na taj se slikovit način izražava ono što kršćani ispovijedaju u vjeri: da su **Otac i Sin iste božanske naravi**, da su istobitni.
sections.subtitle_en: The Throne and the Lamb: An Image of the Consubstantiality of the Father and the Son
sections.screenshot_description_en: Fra Domagoj Runje interprets the relationship of the One who sits on the throne and the Lamb
sections.content_en:
The multitude stands before the throne and before the Lamb. Fra Domagoj Runje draws attention to a motif running through the entire Book of Revelation: when speaking of the heavenly, divine throne, **the One who sits on the throne** and **the Lamb**, who is equal to Him, are mentioned. To both, namely, the **same honor** is always rendered.

All who bow down before the One who sits on the throne bow down also before the Lamb. The host emphasizes that there is no text in which the Lamb would bow down to the One on the throne. In that vivid way is expressed what Christians profess in faith: that the **Father and the Son are of the same divine nature**, that they are consubstantial.

sections.subtitle: Haljine ubijeljene u krvi: paradoks spasenja
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj objašnjava paradoksalnu sliku haljina ubijeljenih u krvi Jaganjčevoj
sections.content:
Mnoštvo u bijelim haljinama pjeva hvalospjev „Spasenje Bogu našemu koji sjedi na prijestolju i Jaganjcu“. Fra Domagoj Runje objašnjava da se time želi reći kako **spasenje pripada Bogu i Jaganjcu**: spašeni nisu spasili sami sebe, nego ih je spasio Bog, i to **krvlju Jaganjčevom**, odnosno krvlju Gospodina Isusa Krista.

Ti isti ljudi kasnije su opisani kao oni koji su došli iz velike nevolje i oprali svoje haljine te ih ubijelili u krvi Jaganjčevoj. Voditelj tu prepoznaje **paradoksalnu sliku**, što u knjizi Otkrivenja nije nimalo neobično. Krv je crvene boje, a ovdje se njome haljine izbjeljuju. Slika poručuje da je krv Jaganjčeva te ljude **očistila od svih grijeha, slabosti i mana** i učinila ih potpuno prikladnima za život u božanskom svijetu, koji simbolizira bijela boja.

**Palme** u kršćanskoj tradiciji i ikonografiji redovito simboliziraju mučenike, koji se prikazuju s palmom u ruci. No fra Domagoj naglašava da se u ovom kontekstu prizor ne odnosi nužno samo na one koji su prolili krv svjedočeći vjeru u Isusa Krista. Odnosi se na **sve kršćane**, sve krštene koji su u krštenju obukli bijele haljine. Kršćanski je život izazovan i puno je životnih borbi i nevolja kroz koje treba proći da bi se došlo u kraljevstvo Božje. U širem smislu, dakle, riječ je o svima koji su ustrajali u tim borbama.
sections.subtitle_en: Robes Whitened in Blood: The Paradox of Salvation
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host explains the paradoxical image of robes whitened in the blood of the Lamb
sections.content_en:
The multitude in white robes sings the hymn of praise “Salvation belongs to our God who sits on the throne and to the Lamb”. Fra Domagoj Runje explains that this is intended to say how **salvation belongs to God and the Lamb**: the saved did not save themselves, but God saved them, and that **by the blood of the Lamb**, that is, by the blood of the Lord Jesus Christ.

Those same people are later described as those who have come out of the great tribulation and have washed their robes and whitened them in the blood of the Lamb. The host recognizes here a **paradoxical image**, which in the Book of Revelation is not at all unusual. Blood is red in color, and here robes are whitened with it. The image conveys that the blood of the Lamb **cleansed** these people **from all sins, weaknesses, and flaws** and made them completely suitable for life in the divine world, which is symbolized by the white color.

**Palm branches** in Christian tradition and iconography regularly symbolize martyrs, who are depicted with a palm in hand. But fra Domagoj emphasizes that in this context the scene does not necessarily refer only to those who shed blood witnessing faith in Jesus Christ. It refers to **all Christians**, all the baptized who in baptism put on white robes. Christian life is challenging and there are many life struggles and tribulations through which one must pass in order to enter the kingdom of God. In a broader sense, therefore, it is about all who persevered in those struggles.

sections.subtitle: Znak Tau: pečat u obliku križa
sections.screenshot_description: Fra Domagoj Runje objašnjava znak Tau iz knjige proroka Ezekiela
sections.content:
Pečat kojim su obilježene sluge Božje, objašnjava fra Domagoj Runje, „posuđen“ je iz **knjige proroka Ezekiela**, gdje su spašenici opečaćeni **znakom Tau**.

Riječ *Tau* najprije znači „znak“. Kako je taj znak izgledao, zna onaj tko poznaje **paleohebrejski, odnosno starohebrejski alfabet**. U njemu Tau nije izgledao kao u današnjem hebrejskom pismu, nego je imao **oblik križa**, sličniji današnjem slovu X. Bio je jednostavan i lako pamtljiv, pa su ga kršćani prepoznali kao **simbol Kristova križa**.

Opečaćene sluge Boga, zaključuje voditelj, oni su koji su obilježeni znakom križa. Na čelima ne nose neko drugo ime, pa čak ni svoje, nego **ime i znak Boga našega**. Na njihovim čelima i u njihovu životu prepoznatljivo je da su kršćani.
sections.subtitle_en: The Sign of the Tau: A Seal in the Shape of a Cross
sections.screenshot_description_en: Fra Domagoj Runje explains the sign of the Tau from the Book of the Prophet Ezekiel
sections.content_en:
The seal with which the servants of God are marked, explains fra Domagoj Runje, is “borrowed” from the **Book of the Prophet Ezekiel**, where the saved are sealed with the **sign of the Tau**.

The word *Tau* primarily means “sign”. What that sign looked like is known to whoever knows the **Paleo-Hebrew, that is, Old Hebrew alphabet**. In it, Tau did not look as it does in today's Hebrew script, but had the **shape of a cross**, more similar to today's letter X. It was simple and easy to remember, so Christians recognized it as a **symbol of Christ's cross**.

The sealed servants of God, the host concludes, are those marked with the sign of the cross. On their foreheads they do not carry some other name, not even their own, but the **name and sign of our God**. On their foreheads and in their life it is recognizable that they are Christians.

sections.subtitle: Čovjek, vol, lav i orao: cijelo stvorenje slavi Boga
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj tumači simboliku četiriju bića oko Božjega prijestolja
sections.content:
Među likovima odlomka nalaze se i **četiri bića**, poznata iz prethodnih poglavlja knjige Otkrivenja, ali i iz knjige proroka Ezekiela. Jedno ima lice čovjeka, drugo lice vola, treće lice lava, a četvrto lice orla.

Fra Domagoj Runje podsjeća da se ti likovi danas koriste kao **simboli četvorice evanđelista**. U izvornom biblijskom kontekstu, međutim, oni označuju **sva stvorena živa bića**:

- biće s licem **čovjeka**: čovječanstvo,
- biće s licem **vola**: domaće životinje,
- biće s licem **lava**: divlje životinje ili zvijeri,
- biće s licem **orla**: ptice, krilate životinje.

Poruka je, prema voditelju, da **sva živa bića slave Boga**. Četiri bića zajedno sa starješinama klanjaju se pred prijestoljem Božjim i Jaganjčevim padajući licem na zemlju, što je izraz štovanja, i pjevaju: „Blagoslov i slava i mudrost i zahvalnica i čast i moć i snaga Bogu našemu u vijeke vjekova. Amen.“
sections.subtitle_en: Man, Ox, Lion, and Eagle: All Creation Praises God
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host interprets the symbolism of the four living creatures around God's throne
sections.content_en:
Among the characters of the passage are also the **four living creatures**, known from the previous chapters of the Book of Revelation, but also from the Book of the Prophet Ezekiel. One has the face of a man, the second the face of an ox, the third the face of a lion, and the fourth the face of an eagle.

Fra Domagoj Runje recalls that these figures are used today as **symbols of the four evangelists**. In the original biblical context, however, they designate **all created living beings**:

- the creature with the face of a **man**: humanity,
- the creature with the face of an **ox**: domestic animals,
- the creature with the face of a **lion**: wild animals or beasts,
- the creature with the face of an **eagle**: birds, winged animals.

The message, according to the host, is that **all living beings praise God**. The four living creatures together with the elders fall prostrate before the throne of God and of the Lamb, which is an expression of reverence, and sing: “Blessing and glory and wisdom and thanksgiving and honor and power and strength to our God forever and ever. Amen.”

sections.subtitle: Posljednja riječ pripada dobru
sections.screenshot_description: Fra Domagoj Runje izriče temeljnu poruku knjige Otkrivenja o pobjedi dobra
sections.content:
Navedeni hvalospjev samo je jedan od mnogih kratkih hvalospjeva kojima je knjiga Otkrivenja prožeta i koji, ističe fra Domagoj Runje, **unaprijed govore o Božjoj pobjedi** u ovom svijetu.

Knjiga sadrži i mnoge prizore zala u ljudskoj povijesti: od **prirodnih katastrofa** poput potresa i gladi, do ratova i raznih **moralnih katastrofa**, među kojima su opet ratovi i drugi sukobi među ljudima. Ipak, kroz opise svih tih zala provlače se **hvalospjevi pobjede**, koji poručuju da posljednja riječ nije riječ zla, nego dobra.

Temeljnu poruku knjige Otkrivenja voditelj sažima ovako: unaprijed nam je rečeno da će **pobijediti dobro**, a na ovom smo svijetu pozvani **svrstati se na stranu pobjednika**.
sections.subtitle_en: The Last Word Belongs to the Good
sections.screenshot_description_en: Fra Domagoj Runje utters the fundamental message of the Book of Revelation about the victory of good
sections.content_en:
The mentioned hymn of praise is only one of many short hymns of praise with which the Book of Revelation is permeated and which, fra Domagoj Runje points out, **speak in advance of God's victory** in this world.

The book also contains many scenes of evils in human history: from **natural disasters** such as earthquakes and famine, to wars and various **moral catastrophes**, among which are again wars and other conflicts among people. Nevertheless, through the descriptions of all those evils run **hymns of victory**, which convey that the last word is not the word of evil, but of good.

The host summarizes the fundamental message of the Book of Revelation like this: we have been told in advance that **good will conquer**, and in this world we are called to **align ourselves on the side of the victor**.

sections.subtitle: Sveci su oni koji su izabrali stranu pobjednika
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj povezuje poruku Otkrivenja sa svetkovinom Svih svetih
sections.content:
Iz te poruke proizlazi i smisao same svetkovine. Na Sve svete, kaže fra Domagoj Runje, slave se ljudi koji su, **bilo kanonizirani bilo ne**, za svoga zemaljskog života **stali na stranu pobjednika**.

Oni sada pjevaju pobjedničke pjesme u kraljevstvu nebeskom i slave Boga pred prijestoljem Božjim i Jaganjčevim. Upravo su oni neizbrojivo mnoštvo iz 7. poglavlja knjige Otkrivenja.
sections.subtitle_en: The Saints Are Those Who Chose the Side of the Victor
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host connects the message of Revelation with the Solemnity of All Saints
sections.content_en:
From that message also arises the meaning of the solemnity itself. On All Saints, says fra Domagoj Runje, people are celebrated who, **whether canonized or not**, during their earthly life **stood on the side of the victor**.

They now sing songs of victory in the kingdom of heaven and praise God before the throne of God and of the Lamb. It is precisely they who are the innumerable multitude from Chapter 7 of the Book of Revelation.

sections.subtitle: Svijeće na grobovima kao molitva za pokojne
sections.screenshot_description: Fra Domagoj Runje govori o Dušnom danu i običaju pohoda grobovima
sections.content:
Uz svetkovinu Svih svetih, u tradiciji i u crkvenom kalendaru, vezan je **spomen svih vjernih mrtvih**, koji se slavi **2. studenoga**. Fra Domagoj Runje napominje da vjernici, prema ustaljenoj praksi, grobove svojih pokojnika obilaze već **1. studenoga**, na samu svetkovinu Svih svetih.

Tada pale svijeće i kite grobove cvijećem. Na taj način, objašnjava voditelj, izražavaju ljubav prema pokojnicima. Ta se ljubav sastoji u **želji da se svi koji su prije njih otišli u vječnu domovinu pridruže broju opečaćenih slugu Božjih**, neizbrojivom mnoštvu koje pred prijestoljem Božjim i Jaganjčevim pjeva pobjedničke hvalospjeve.
sections.subtitle_en: Candles on Graves as Prayer for the Deceased
sections.screenshot_description_en: Fra Domagoj Runje speaks about All Souls' Day and the custom of visiting graves
sections.content_en:
Along with the Solemnity of All Saints, in tradition and in the church calendar, the **commemoration of all the faithful departed** is linked, which is celebrated on **November 2nd**. Fra Domagoj Runje notes that the faithful, according to established practice, visit the graves of their deceased already on **November 1st**, on the Solemnity of All Saints itself.

Then they light candles and adorn graves with flowers. In that way, the host explains, they express love toward the deceased. That love consists in the **desire that all who departed before them to the eternal homeland join the number of the sealed servants of God**, the innumerable multitude that sings hymns of victory before the throne of God and of the Lamb.
